label: conj:q-gl-classical-limit
title: Classical limit of the $q$-Geometric Langlands correspondence
html:
Any q-deformation of Geometric Langlands must reduce to the classical Beilinson–Drinfeld equivalence \mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{BD}} at q = 1; the q-correspondence passes this consistency check, and it does so through three compatible limits of its defining data (differential, Hecke, and dual-group). Accordingly, as q \to 1 in the \mathbb{G}_m-family, the q-Geometric Langlands correspondence recovers the classical Geometric Langlands equivalence:

  \lim_{q \to 1} \mathbb{L}_q =  \mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{BD}}
  \colon \mathcal{D}\text{-}\mathrm{mod}(\mathrm{Bun}_G(X))
  \xrightarrow{ \sim }
  \mathrm{QCoh}(\mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}}(X)).

We factor this degeneration into three limits:

  1. Differential limit: d_q \to d and d_q^2 \to 0 (non-vanishing of d_q^2). Quantum flat connections become classical flat connections. Quantum local systems become classical local systems.
  2. Hecke limit: The Hecke relation (T-q)(T+q^{-1}) = 0 degenerates to (T-1)(T+1) = 0. This recovers the symmetric group action. Quantum Hecke operators become classical Hecke correspondences.
  3. Dual group limit: \check{G}_q = G_{q^{-1}}^\vee \to G^\vee = \check{G} as the quantum deformation vanishes.
heading: Conjecture
